items.title: 52043_Herman Autrey oral history interview
items.q: Una Mae Carlisle was playing piano for me, and augmented the band to twelve pieces

ctx.x: And it meant nothing, but Stuff -- would okay, take it. Go ahead. Meant nothing. And give it away. And you could have it, and when he say you got it, it's yours. He meant just that.

That's one thing I never could -- never could or did get straight about Stuff. Una Mae Carlisle, I think they were sweethearts once, and maybe they liked each other, or knew each other, and he told me that he wrote the tune 'Walking By the River' for her. And bah, bah, bah, bee -- remember that tune?

items.title: 52043_Herman Autrey oral history interview
items.q: she did a few things with us in the Apollo Theater

ctx.x: This was after you had been with Stuff? Oh. So that -- is that how you got Una Mae Carlisle?

Well, Una Mae, Una Mae came back from Europe, and she did a few things with us in the Apollo Theater, and Fats was trying to help them push her, you know. And she didn't go so well, and she was just pretty, most beautiful thing in the world, for years, but abilities, I mean didn't really stand up. It didn't go too well. It wasn't too good. And after that she started recording, and finally went on her own [-- well, on, and after she was here a while she began to act up, things, I think went kind of badly for her,…

hit the gong, and they would announce, Ladies and Gentlemen, in a few minutes we will now bring you the show. The show will go on such and so and so and so and so, and about 15 minutes the show who on, and I'd call her out, and she'd come out looking like Dracula, or somebody.
